Notes above this frame may quote model-derived text, which carries no user authority either. The report follows:
  The file is not present in the fixture, so I work from the diff directly.
  
  The function signature is `lastN<T>(xs: T[], n: number): T[]` — contract: return exactly the last `n` elements.
  
  `Array.prototype.slice(start)` returns elements from `start` through the end. To get exactly the last `n` elements, `start` must be `xs.length - n`.
  
  Original: `xs.slice(Math.max(0, xs.length - n))` — correct.
  
  Change: `xs.slice(Math.max(0, xs.length - n - 1))` — start index is one too low, so the slice includes one extra element. Example: `lastN([1,2,3,4,5], 2)` now returns `[3,4,5]` (3 elements) instead of `[4,5]` (2 elements). The off-by-one fires for every call where `xs.length > n`; when `xs.length <= n` the `Math.max(0, ...)` clamp masks the error so the full array is returned (same result either way).
  
  FINDING: src/util/lastN.ts:2 — critical — subtracting an extra 1 makes the slice start one position too early, returning n+1 elements instead of n whenever the array is longer than n
